deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics and is not a Riemann manuscript. It is page 379 of a printed text in Fraktur type. The surrounding pages place it in the annual report (Jahresbericht) of the Königliche Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen, printed in the 'Nachrichten von der G. A. Universität und der K. Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften' for 1863. The report contains obituaries of foreign members who died that year: Mitscherlich on 28 Aug, Jacob Grimm on 20 Sept and J. F. Böhmer on 22 Oct, all 1863.

The page continues the obituary of the chemist Eilhard Mitscherlich. Its claims, in order:
(1) His discovery of isomorphism gave crystallography new importance for chemistry. Crystal forms gave a basis for fixing the atomic weights of a compound's constituents.
(2) Isomorphism mattered greatly for mineralogy and influenced the classification of minerals. It reconciled crystal forms with chemical composition, as Berzelius later did in his second mineral system.
(3) Berzelius happened to be in Berlin, met Mitscherlich, and let him work for several years in his private laboratory in Stockholm.
(4) In 1821 Mitscherlich succeeded Klaproth as professor of chemistry at the University of Berlin and was made a member of the Berlin Academy.
(5) Despite other offices, he kept up wide-ranging research. The page singles out his work on the specific gravities of gases and vapours and their relation to atomic weights, and his discoveries of selenic acid, benzene and dimorphism. It praises his original methods, exact observation and rigorous argument.

The pencil mark '11' in the right margin is an archival foliation (Bl. 11). It shows that a printed leaf, perhaps part of an offprint or Nachrichten issue, was filed in the 'R.Primzahlen' bundle. There are no derivations, formulas or mathematical notes by Riemann or anyone else on the page.
errors: No mathematical content, so there is nothing to check mathematically.

Historical nuance: Mitscherlich was appointed extraordinary professor in Berlin in 1821 and ordinary professor in 1825. His Academy membership dates from 1822, so 'schon 1821' compresses events slightly.
Historical nuance: Klaproth had died in 1817, so 'an Klaproth's Stelle' means succeeding to his chair rather than a direct handover.
Previous-page context: born 7 Jan 1794 and died 28 Aug 1863, he died at age 69, i.e. in his 70th year. 'Im 69. Lebensjahre' is therefore slightly inexact by the strict ordinal reading.
Previous-page context: the first name is properly 'Eilhard' (variant 'Eilert'), not 'Eilart'.

results.what: Biographical/obituary statement on Mitscherlich's discovery of isomorphism and its significance for atomic weights and mineral classification
Mention of Mitscherlich's discoveries of selenic acid, benzene (from benzoic acid, 1834) and dimorphism, and his vapour-density work
results.modern_name: History of chemistry (selenic acid 1827, benzene synthesis 1834, polymorphism/dimorphism)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed obituary of the chemist Mitscherlich from the 1863 Göttingen Nachrichten. It has no mathematical content and nothing by Riemann. Its only interest is archival: a printed leaf filed in the 'R.Primzahlen' bundle.

checkable.asserts: Mitscherlich, born 1794 and died 1863, died at age 69 (before or after his birthday), consistent with the obituary's age statement up to ordinal convention.
Jacob Grimm (born 4 Jan 1785, died 20 Sept 1863) died aged 78, i.e. 'im 79. Lebensjahre', as stated on the next page.

transcription_corrections: 'Zusammeuhang' (line 8) faithfully reproduces a printer's error in the original (turned 'n'); the intended word is 'Zusammenhang'.
In 'Er gestattete ihm in sei=' the print appears to read 'iu' (turned 'n') for 'in'; the sense is 'in'.
The marginal pencil mark at right reads '11' (possibly with a preceding stroke, '-11'), the archival leaf number, not part of the printed text.
